relevance_note: The paper describes a mother (P1) and daughter (P2) with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant, stated as a 'missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (main text, Table 1, figure legends, Supplementary Table 1 and supplementary figure legends) and built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory; every value was chosen by me from reading, and the script only resolved typed quotes to the exact paper characters (the paper uses U+2005 spaces in 'c.608T > G' and 'IgA < 0.06', curly apostrophes and an en dash in '13–17'). Table 1 has patients as rows; the P1 row contains a line break inside the Igs cell, so P1 row spans that run past that cell include the newline. Labels: the paper uses 'P1'/'P2' most often (also 'Patient 1'/'patient 1', 'D001'/'D002' in Fig. 2 and Suppl. Table 1). In scope: P1 (mother), P2 (daughter), the brother of P1 (figure 1 legend: deceased at 40, rheumatism and thyroid disease, not tested), and L001, a 'CVID patient control with TNFAIP3 LoF mutation c.1309del (p.Ala437Profs)' used in the immunoblots; L001 is included because the paper attributes a TNFAIP3 variant to that person, with no further clinical detail. Healthy controls (HC1-3, H1, H2) are out of scope. Not recorded as a variant: the heterozygous TNFRSF13B c.310T > C (p.Cys104Arg) in the mother, because the paper calls it 'a known risk factor' (risk allele rule); the Discussion says it is absent in the daughter. No proband or index case is named (WES was done on the mother's DNA and segregation analysis in the daughter), so is_proband is null for P1 and P2. Inheritance in P2 is left 'not reported': both carry the variant and segregation was done in the daughter, but the paper never states maternal inheritance. Ages of presentation (P1 49 years, P2 29 years) are recorded only as feature onsets, not as age at diagnosis or last evaluation, because the paper gives no age at HA20 diagnosis or last evaluation. Vital status of P1 and P2 left 'not reported' (only 'in stable remission' is stated). Variant type for L001 left 'not reported' (authors say 'LoF mutation', not a class). Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) Table 1 gives P1 'Age at onset 18 years', but the text reports 'a childhood history of oral and genital ulcers'; (2) Table 1 gives P2 'Age at onset 9 years', but the text says ulcers 'since adolescence'. Both table onset values are recorded as stated. (3) P1's CT angiography showed the iliac occlusion 'without features typical of vasculitis', while a skin biopsy showed leucocytoclastic vasculitis; I recorded the CT negative as a narrow imaging finding and did not treat it as excluding vasculitis, so the vasculitis checklist item stays observed. Checklist judgements: P1 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' marked observed from 'a bout of gastroenteritis' (may have been infectious); P1 'recurrent fever' not reported (one bout of high fever); P1 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' not reported (leukopenia not attributed to autoimmunity; pernicious anemia not treated as an autoimmune cytopenia); P2 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' not reported (diarrhea only); P2 'type 1 diabetes' not reported although the paper states 'no signs of insulin deficiency' (not an explicit statement about diabetes); brother of P1: 'rheumatism' not mapped to arthritis or arthralgia and 'thyroid disease' not mapped to autoimmune thyroiditis. Rituximab-related B-cell depletion in P1 was not recorded as a phenotypic feature (treatment effect).

our findings revealed higher levels of p65 NF-κB phosphorylation in CD4+ and CD14+ cells from patients compared to the HC

we have identified a novel pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3 associated with HA20
indicating a likely pathogenic variant effect
